script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Romance
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

Title: THE DREAM COLLIDES

INT. LOS ANGELES APARTMENT - NIGHT

A cozy one-bedroom apartment, filled with warm yellow light. The aroma of freshly baked pasta wafts from the kitchen.

SARAH (30s, passionate, artistic) stands at the counter, adding herbs to a simmering pot. She hums a melody, lost in thought.

Suddenly, there's a knock on the door. Sarah pauses, looks towards it, then back at the pot. She sighs, then puts on an apron and heads to answer it.

INT. APARTMENT HALLWAY - NIGHT

Sarah opens the door to reveal MIKE (30s, ambitious, charismatic), a man she met at a gallery opening weeks ago. He wears a suit and carries a folder.

MIKE
(cheerfully)
Sarah, I'm glad I caught you at home. I've been trying to get in touch with you about the project I told you about earlier.

SARAH
(surprised)
Oh, hi Mike. Yes, come in.

INT. LOS ANGELES APARTMENT - NIGHT

Mike follows Sarah back into the kitchen. She offers him a seat at the table.

MIKE
(eagerly)
So, as I mentioned earlier, I work for a publishing company. We've been looking for a new author to headline our annual literary festival. I believe you have what it takes.

SARAH
(hesitant)
Me? I'm just a waitress and a part-time artist.

MIKE
(excitedly)
Exactly! You have a unique voice and perspective that would capture the hearts of readers. But, to do so, you need to focus on your writing full-time.

SARAH
(doubtful)
I don't know if I can afford that. Rent, groceries... I barely make ends meet as it is.

MIKE
(smiling)
That's where I come in. I can offer you a substantial advance on your first book, enough to cover your expenses for at least six months. In exchange, I'll need a percentage of the royalties.

SARAH
(considering)
That's a big risk, Mike. What if I can't write a book that sells?

MIKE
(confidently)
With your talent, I don't think that's a concern. But, even if it doesn't work out, it's a chance worth taking, isn't it?

SARAH
(pensive)
I suppose so... But, I can't just abandon my job and my apartment without any notice.

MIKE
(sincerely)
I understand, but I can help you with that. I can put you in touch with a few people who can help you find an affordable place to stay while you work on your book. And, I can help you negotiate a severance package from your current job.

SARAH
(impressed)
Wow, you're really serious about this.

MIKE
(nods)
Absolutely. I believe in you and your talent, Sarah. And, I think this could be the opportunity of a lifetime.

INT. LOS ANGELES APARTMENT - DAYS LATER

Sarah's apartment is now empty. She stands in the middle of an unfurnished room, surrounded by stacks of books and papers.

SARAH
(to herself)
I can't believe I'm doing this.

She takes a deep breath, then pulls out a notebook and pen. She begins to write.

INT. CAFÉ - DAYS LATER

Sarah sits at a table in a busy café, typing away on her laptop. Mike sits across from her, sipping a cup of coffee.

MIKE
(proudly)
You've made great progress, Sarah. I'm impressed.

SARAH
(smiling)
Thank you, Mike. I couldn't have done it without your support.

MIKE
(grinning)
Well, I'm glad I could be of help. And, I have some more good news. I've found a publisher interested in your manuscript.

SARAH
(excitedly)
Really? That soon?

MIKE
(nods)
Yes, but they want some revisions first. I'll help you with that.

SARAH
(gratefully)
Thank you, Mike. I don't know what I'd do without you.

MIKE
(smiling)
That's what friends are for.

INT. PUBLISHER'S OFFICE - WEEKS LATER

Sarah and Mike sit in a plush office, facing a stern PUBLISHER (50s, stern, but fair).

PUBLISHER
(sternly)
Your manuscript shows promise, Sarah, but there are some areas that need improvement. I suggest you rework the ending and strengthen the character development.

SARAH
(determined)
I will, sir. Thank you for the opportunity.

MIKE
(firmly)
We'll make it work.

INT. LOS ANGELES APARTMENT - MONTHS LATER

Sarah's apartment is now filled with books and awards. She sits at her desk, typing away on her laptop, a smile on her face.

MIKE enters, carrying a stack of papers.

MIKE
(proudly)
Looks like your hard work paid off, Sarah. The manuscript is a hit.

SARAH
(gratefully)
I couldn't have done it without you, Mike.

MIKE
(smiling)
I'm just glad I could help.

SARAH
(serious)
But, Mike, I owe you more than just royalties. I owe you my dream.

MIKE
(surprised)
What do you mean?

SARAH
(determined)
I mean, I want to pay you back for your faith in me, for your support, and for your friendship. I want to use my success to help other aspiring writers.

MIKE
(impressed)
Sarah, that's an amazing gesture. I'll gladly accept your offer.

SARAH
(smiling)
Good. Then, let's get to work.

INT. LOS ANGELES LITERARY FESTIVAL - DAYS LATER

Sarah stands on stage, surrounded by applause. Mike sits in the audience, beaming with pride.

SARAH
(speaking into the microphone)
Thank you all for coming today. It's an honor to be here, sharing my story with you. But, this isn't just my story. It's the story of every aspiring writer out there who believes in the power of their dreams.

MIKE
(whispering to himself)
She did it.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
